value.body: A postgraduate degree in analytics or business analytics that combines statistics, programming (Python, R, SQL), machine learning and business problem-solving. Universities offer it as an M.Sc; similar content also appears as an MBA (Business Analytics) or a PG diploma.

items.label: Core subjects
items.value: Statistics, programming, machine learning, data visualisation, business applications

items.label: Research & insights industry workforce
items.note: One of several sectors that hire analytics graduates; industry size ~USD 3.2 billion
items.source: Market Research Society of India (MRSI) industry report (as reported)

value.title: How you get in
value.body: A bachelor's degree, often with mathematics or statistics at Class 12 or degree level (rules vary). Admission is through CUET-PG, a university or institute entrance test, or merit and interview. BBA graduates usually show quantitative ability through the entrance test.

value.title: At a glance
items: Programme names vary — analytics, business analytics, data analytics — so the syllabus says more than the title.
Fees vary widely between public universities and private institutes.
Common first roles are data analyst, business analyst and reporting analyst.
Hiring weighs projects, internships and tool skills alongside the degree.
